Wing + gable, on the ground

Bedroom wing and a gabled living pavilion at an angle, on piles, with the garage tucked under the west deck. Both schemes align to the same two points, so once you have calibrated one the other lands in the same place.

Checking whether this phone can do AR…

01Calibrate on site

The model has no idea where it is until you tell it. You give it two points whose position it already knows — it solves the heading and the position from those, then holds still while you walk.

  1. 1

    Tap “Stand it up at full size” and allow the camera. Sweep slowly at the ground until the blue ring appears.

  2. 2

    Pick point 1 and walk to it — a GPS readout in the panel counts you down. Stand on it, put the ring on your feet, tap Set point 1.

  3. 3

    Pick point 2. Either walk to it and tap Walk, or stay put, aim the phone straight at it and tap Sight. Sighting is for things you can see but not stand on — a neighbour’s roof corner. Behind you is fine; just turn round.

  4. 4

    It places itself and reports a check figure: the distance between your two points as walked, against the distance on the plan. If those disagree by more than a metre or so, something moved — re-align.

  5. 5

    Nudge to trim — 0.2° and 0.25 m steps. Then walk it. Re-align whenever it looks like it has slipped.

Pick the two points as far apart as you can. Heading error is what throws the far end of the building, and a 40 m baseline is four times better than a 10 m one. A 1° error puts the south end of the living wing 0.7 m out.

Add your own points. Tap + add a point, give it a name, and paste coordinates from Google Maps — long-press the spot in satellite view and tap the numbers to copy. Your rock, a fence post, a stump. They are saved on this phone.

Standing on the mark, the bedroom floor reads about 0.3 m above your feet. Walk north-east and the ground climbs into a cut over head height; walk south-west and it lifts onto piles until the deck is 3.6 m up.
